findings.compatibility_reason: Any external module or plugin that calls ratelimitAddConfig directly and was compiled against the old signature will fail to compile or link with the new signature. findings.uncertainty: No uncertainty. The signature change is unambiguous - 2 trailing sbool parameters were added to a function declared in a public header.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no external plugins or consumers of the rsyslog runtime library call ratelimitAddConfig directly.

findings.old_behavior: The action_s struct had pszName as its last field before DEF_ATOMIC_HELPER_MUT(mutCAS), followed by error file fields and then stats counters ending at ctrResume.
findings.new_behavior: The action_s struct has two new fields (pszRatelimitName, ratelimiter) inserted after pszName, and 4 new STATSCOUNTER_DEF fields (ctrRateLimitAllowed, ctrRateLimitDropped, ctrRateLimitPaced, ctrRateLimitPacedUsec) added after ctrResume. The ratelimit_shared_s struct has 3 new fields (scope, output_mode, output_pace_forbidden) inserted before interval, shifting all subsequent field offsets.
findings.compatibility_reason: The action_s and ratelimit_shared_s structs are declared in public headers (action.h, ratelimit.h). Any code compiled against the old struct layouts that directly accesses struct members, uses sizeof(), or relies on field offsets will read incorrect data. Even indirect consumers (e.g., debuggers, core dump analyzers, serialization code) may be affected.

findings.why_not_internal_only: Both action_s and ratelimit_shared_s are defined in public headers shipped with the rsyslog runtime library. Even if direct field access is uncommon, sizeof() changes affect memory allocation, array indexing, and debug symbol matching. The struct layout changes are observable at the binary level.
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. Impact depends on whether external consumers directly access struct members vs using accessor functions.
findings.recommended_review: Check existing plugins for direct struct field access. Verify that the rsyslog SONAME version policy allows struct layout changes in the runtime library.
findings.test_recommendation: Rebuild all modules against the new headers and run full test suite. Verify ABI compatibility through symbol versioning checks if available.

findings.old_behavior: Action stats output contained counters: processed, batchesprocessed, failed, suspended, suspended.duration, resumed
findings.new_behavior: Action stats output now additionally contains 4 new counters: ratelimit.allowed, ratelimit.dropped, ratelimit.paced, ratelimit.paced_usec
findings.compatibility_reason: Any monitoring system, log parser, or tool that consumes rsyslog stats output (CEF/JSON formats) will now see 4 new fields in every action's stats record. While parsers that accept unknown fields gracefully will not break, strict schema validators or tools that enumerate expected fields may fail or produce warnings.
findings.why_not_internal_only: Stats output is a documented, user-facing interface of rsyslog. The stats subsystem formats and emits counter data through multiple output formats (CEE, JSON, ES), and external monitoring tools actively consume this data. The existing test scripts (stats-cee.sh, stats-json.sh, etc.) were all updated in this patch to expect the new fields, confirming the output format is externally visible.
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. New counters are unconditionally registered for every action via actionConstructFinalize. All actions without rate limiting will emit these as zero values, changing the output format for ALL actions.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that downstream monitoring tools accept additional fields in stats output without breaking.
findings.test_recommendation: Run stats output tests (stats-cee.sh, stats-json.sh, stats-json-es.sh, stats-cee-vg.sh, stats-json-vg.sh) to validate that the new counters are emitted with correct zero values for actions without rate limiting, and with expected non-zero values when rate limiting is active.
